records.Concise description: Enterprise Lightning infrastructure company whose current Payments product provides API-driven Lightning payment execution while abstracting liquidity and operational node management.
records.Deeper researched summary: Voltage evolved from hosted Lightning nodes and liquidity tooling toward enterprise payment infrastructure. Voltage Payments went live on mainnet in 2025 with a credit-backed model intended to avoid pre-funding Lightning liquidity; node-backed wallet/infrastructure configurations have also existed. In July-August 2026 the company is sunsetting self-serve infrastructure while continuing to position enterprise Payments as its focus, so public copy must distinguish the active enterprise product from the self-serve hosting being retired.
records.Launch / history: Founded as Lightning node/infrastructure hosting; expanded into liquidity and Payments products. In 2026 it announced retirement of self-serve infrastructure while focusing on enterprise payments.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: Voltage demonstrates that Lightning payment infrastructure can be sold as managed APIs/liquidity/operations rather than as a merchant checkout product or wallet.
Important technical or cultural characte: Credit-backed payment model in Voltage Payments
records.Verification basis: Current official Payments material verifies active enterprise product operation; current migration documentation verifies that self-serve infrastructure is being retired rather than treating all Voltage products as unchanged.
Research notes / uncertainties: Self-serve infrastructure is scheduled for deprovisioning by August 31, 2026; reverify after that date before publishing platform-wide descriptions.
Do not use one custody label for every Voltage configuration; credit-backed Payments and node-backed deployments have different trust models.
Do not call Voltage a merchant processor unless referring to a specific merchant-facing integration.

records.Concise description: Enterprise payments infrastructure company providing Lightning connectivity and broader payment orchestration through managed APIs and its Grid/global-account products.
records.Deeper researched summary: Lightspark Connect abstracts Lightning node, channel, liquidity, routing and operational complexity for enterprises, while the company's newer Grid/global-account stack connects Bitcoin, fiat and stablecoin payment flows. These products do not share one universal custody model: some integrations are managed platform/account infrastructure, while specific wallet integrations can deliver to self-custody. MSC therefore treats Lightspark as one integrated infrastructure company and documents custody at the product/flow level rather than calling the whole company custodial or non-custodial.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2022 around enterprise Lightning infrastructure; subsequently expanded into cross-border/global payment orchestration and account infrastructure.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is a major example of Lightning being embedded beneath enterprise payment APIs rather than exposed as merchant node software.
Important technical or cultural characte: Custody depends on product and integration
records.Verification basis: Current first-party company and documentation surfaces verify active enterprise payment and Lightning infrastructure in 2026.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not collapse Lightspark Connect, Grid and Spark-related integrations into one custody statement.
Stablecoin/fiat capabilities are included only as context for how the company connects Bitcoin payments to other settlement rails.
Do not canonize Spark here as a separate PAYMENTS profile; its protocol/network role belongs under NETWORK if included.

records.Entity / project type: open-source Lightning account and application platform
records.Concise description: Open-source Lightning accounting and application platform that exposes wallets/accounts, APIs and extensions on top of a configurable Lightning or payment funding source.
records.Deeper researched summary: LNbits is not itself a Lightning node implementation. It maintains an accounting layer over a funding source and can expose multiple user wallets, APIs, POS/payment extensions and services. The custody model is deployment-specific: a self-run instance backed by the operator's own LND/CLN can be self-controlled for that operator, while users of a hosted LNbits instance generally trust the instance operator and its funding source; newer alternative backends can have still different trust properties.
Creators / founders: Ben Arc and LNbits open-source contributors
records.Launch / history: Created in the early Lightning application era and developed into a modular server/application layer used for wallets, merchant tools, LNURL services and experiments.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It explains a crucial payment architecture layer between raw Lightning nodes and end-user apps: account/payment functionality can be built as software over many different funding sources.
Important technical or cultural characte: Lightning-only accounting layer over a funding source
Custody/trust inherited from deployment and funding source
records.Verification basis: Current official documentation and active repository verify the platform role and explicitly describe LNbits as an accounting/application layer over configurable funding sources.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call LNbits universally custodial or non-custodial.
Do not classify it as a Lightning implementation or node manager.
A hosted LNbits provider can be custodian to its users even though the software is open-source/self-hostable.

records.Concise description: Bitcoin-focused swap infrastructure for moving value between Lightning and Bitcoin layers using atomic-swap constructions instead of a conventional custodial exchange deposit.
records.Deeper researched summary: Boltz supports submarine, reverse and chain-swap style flows across Bitcoin, Lightning and Liquid and provides APIs/client software for integrations. Its non-custodial design depends on the end user or integrating client controlling the relevant swap keys/secrets; server-side integrations that custody those materials on a user's behalf can change the effective trust model. Boltz is payment connectivity infrastructure rather than a merchant processor.
records.Launch / history: Developed from late-2010s Lightning swap infrastructure and expanded into a broader Bitcoin-layer bridge.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It makes cross-layer payment connectivity practical when sender and receiver are not on the same Bitcoin rail, without requiring every application to manage Lightning liquidity directly.
Important technical or cultural characte: Client-side key control required for strongest non-custodial model
records.Verification basis: Current official site and documentation verify active swap rails and the non-custodial/client-side integration model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe every third-party Boltz integration as non-custodial unless the user controls the swap secrets/keys.
Liquid is a federated sidechain and must not be described as the Bitcoin base layer.
